text:
Jeremy Lauzon's job in Vegas is to make opposing forwards' nights unpleasant, and he's doing it at volume: 98 hits and 37 blocked shots in 25 games, on about 17 minutes a night.

His one goal came Nov. 19 against Dallas, and The Athletic's Jesse Granger described it this way: Lauzon "crushes a slap shot through traffic off the draw." The shot is real, 97.5 mph at the top (95th percentile by NHL EDGE), even if he had 15 goals in 384 games before this season. Two nights earlier Granger noted "an unforced turnover right in front of his own net" that Adin Hill bailed out, the other side of his game.

At five on five Vegas takes 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, about seven points worse than when he sits, and the goals have roughly matched the chances, so luck isn't hiding anything either way. His value has lived on the penalty kill: Evolving-Hockey had him worth 0.9 wins above replacement last season, 76th among 215 defensemen, with the biggest piece (+2.7 goals) shorthanded. The five-on-five share is the part of his game to watch.
